questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

__From__ all her birthday presents, Vanya liked the alphabetical mat the most.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Amongst**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate substitute for the given sentence is '**Amongst**'.
 
• **Among** and **amongst** are prepositions.
 
• **'Among' **means ‘in the middle or included in a larger group of people or things’. **Among** is commonly followed by a plural noun phrase.
 
• **'Amongst'** is sometimes used as an alternative to among. It is more formal and less common.
 
• It indicates a division, choice, or differentiation involving three or more participants.
 
 
• *Example: The results show that both girls are **amongst** the top 10% of students in the whole school.*
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** ***Amongst** all her birthday presents, Vanya liked the alphabetical mat the most.* 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__**

 
• दिए गए वाक्य के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त विकल्प '**Amongst**' है।
 
• '**Among**' और '**amongst**' में **prepositions** हैं।
 
• '**Among**' का अर्थ है 'बीच में या लोगों या चीजों के बड़े समूह में शामिल'। 'Among' में आमतौर पर plural noun phrase होता है।
 
• '**Amongst**' में कभी-कभी बीच के विकल्प के रूप में प्रयोग किया जाता है। यह अधिक औपचारिक और कम सामान्य है।
 
• 
 
 
• *Example: The results show that both girls are **amongst** the top 10% of students in the whole school.*
 
 
 
• अत: सही उत्तर **विकल्प 1** है।

questions.question: What will be the compound interest on a sum of ₹ 15,000 at the interest rate of 8% per annum in one year, interest compounded semi-annually?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For **semi-annual compounding**, the rate becomes 8% ÷ 2 = 4% and time periods n = 2.

Effective **Interest Rate** for 2 periods = 4 + 4 + (4 × 4)/100 = 8.16%.

**Compound Interest** = 15,000 × 8.16% = 15,000 × 0.0816 = 1,224.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 1,224.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹ 15,000

**Annual Rate (R)** = 8%

**Time (T)** = 1 year

**Formula Used:** Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ; Compound Interest (CI) = A − P

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fa119948ab3f7bfc4676af1a06b6a4ba91e56745ddf72fe9e96119b9265a86f7.png] 

Since interest is **compounded semi-annually**:

⇒ Half-yearly rate (r) = 8% ÷ 2 = 4%

⇒ Number of periods (n) = 1 year × 2 = 2

⇒ A = 15,000 × (1 + 4/100)²

⇒ A = 15,000 × (1.04)²

⇒ A = 15,000 × 1.0816

⇒ A = 16,224

⇒ CI = 16,224 − 15,000

⇒ CI = 1,224

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 1,224.**

**__Additional Information__**

Semi-annual Compounding Rule

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the **annual rate** is divided by 2 and the **time** in years is multiplied by 2.

Effective Rate of Interest

For two successive periods with rate r%, the **effective rate** is given by the formula: r + r + (r²/100)%.

CI vs SI Difference

The difference between CI and SI for 2 periods is P × (r/100)². In this case, the difference is 15,000 × (4/100)² = ₹ 24.

questions.question: A certain sum doubles itself on simple interest in 10 years. At the same rate of interest in how many years it will become 3 times of itself?

We know, Simple interest = (p × r × t)/100

Let, total amount = x

Total simple interest when doubles (S.I. 1) = 2x - x = x

Total simple interest when money becomes three times (S.I. 2) = 3x - x = 2x

Here, (S.I. 2)/(S.I. 1) = 2x/x = 2

So, time required = 2 × 10 = **20 years** [∵ S.I. ∝ Time (All other parameters are constant)]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The time is taken for a certain sum doubles itself on simple interest = 10 years

Simple interest = (p × r × t)/100

Where, p = Total sum of amount

r = Rate of interest

t = Time (years)

**Calculation:**

Let, the total amount = x

The amount becomes after doubles = 2x

The total simple interest = 2x - x = x

So, x = (x × r × 10)/100

⇒ r/10 = 100

⇒ r = 100/10 = 10

∴ The rate of interest = 10%

The total amount becomes after 3 times = 3x

∴ The simple interest = 3x - x = 2x

Let, the required time = T

So, 2x = (x × 10 × T)/100

⇒ 10T = 200

⇒ T = 200/10 = 20

**∴ The certain sum will become 3 times of itself in 20 years**

• Vallabhacharya (1479–1531) founded it in the early 16th century, and it is dedicated to Krishna.
 
• Pushtimarg, a bhakti (devotional) school, was expanded by Vallabhacharya's followers, particularly Gusainji.
